summary.oneLiner: Operationally the best quarter Bandhan has had in a while — PAT INR502cr (+35%), credit cost down to 1.8% from 2.0%, GNPA at 3.1%, secured book now 57% of advances and non-EEB two-thirds of the loan book — yet management **cut its headline ROA guidance from 1.6–1.8% to 1.2–1.4% at exit-Q4 FY27**, attributing the entire 40bps reduction to external factors: ~30bps from funding costs killing the planned NIM expansion to 6.5%, and ~10bps from technology costs inflated by Middle East supply-chain disruption (IT spend up 65% YoY). The internal turnaround is real and improving; the external environment took the earnings target away.

> Adjustments / one-offs: (a) **INR61cr one-time gratuity provision** from the new wage code — management confirmed it will not repeat; adjusting for it, ROA is ~1.1%. (b) Prior-year non-interest income carried ~INR250cr of treasury gains; adjusted growth was +22%. (c) Balance-sheet clean-up actions this quarter: **INR291cr of housing NPAs sold to an ARC** (bringing ~INR120cr of cash recovery, which inflates the reported recovery/upgrade number) and a **INR597cr technical write-off** — both flatter headline GNPA. (d) Deposit growth of 7% understates the franchise; bulk was cut deliberately while retail grew 16%.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **ROA — the headline change. Cut from 1.6–1.8% to 1.2–1.4% at exit-Q4 FY27.** The CFO broke the 40bps down explicitly: **~30bps from NIM** (the bank had "line of sight towards a 6.5% by the end of Q4FY27"; that is now abandoned) and **~10bps from opex** (opex-to-assets guided at 4.2%, already running 4.3%). The medium-term 1.6–1.8% aspiration is **retained but the timeline extended** — "the realization of this aspiration could extend beyond the time line we had originally envisaged."
- **NIM: hold ~6.2%.** No further upside is being built in — "it will be a great achievement for the bank to hold on to the NIMs that we have achieved during this particular quarter." Savings-bank cost of funds has already risen ~20–25bps QoQ despite no repo increase.
- **Credit cost: 1.6–1.8% guidance MAINTAINED** — explicitly not changed, with further marginal improvement expected. EEB credit cost at 3.3% is "very close to the guidance."
- **Credit growth FY27: 14% overall**, comprising **EEB 5–10%** and **non-EEB 20%+**. Q1 tracked ahead at 16% overall and 27% non-EEB; EEB is the laggard at flat.
- **Portfolio mix targets:** EEB capped at **33–35%** of the book; **40% unsecured / 60% secured**.
- **Other income: 10–20bps of ROA improvement expected** — one of only two identified levers left to close the gap to 1.4%.
- **Opex: 4.2% of assets** targeted (4.3% now). **IT cost to remain within 10% of opex** (currently ~8%, ~9.5% including depreciation, against a mature-bank benchmark of 10%), then "slowly bring it down to 8%" as it delivers value. **Cost-to-income (~62%) to stay flat for about a year and taper from FY28.**
- **Technology payback: ~18 months** — "after 18 months or so, we should see the outcome of all of this coming in the form of productivity gains."
- **Credit card launch expected in Q2 FY27** — "we are just waiting to be launched… probably in this quarter."
- **PSL compliance of the MFI book** (currently 40%) to be dialled up — "post this quarter, we will be comfortably placed in terms of PSL."
- **DSA dependency to fall as branch sourcing scales** — branch-channel asset sourcing has gone from ~INR200cr/month to **over INR900cr in the last quarter**.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable. The forward-growth constraint is deliberate: EEB growth is being throttled at 5–10% because of external risk rather than demand, and management repeated that it will not repeat past mistakes — "we do not want to suddenly jump very aggressively what we have did in the past and then burnt our fingers." FCNR-B mobilisation, which the sector is counting on for funding relief, has been negligible here: **only INR30cr raised**.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **EEB / microfinance** — INR52,641cr, roughly flat, with the customary Q1 seasonal decline much shallower than prior years. Yields were hiked **100bps in February 2026** and not since. Management stressed a rebuilt operating model: "a new model has been put into place with a lot of guardrails and also new credit underwriting system." Vintage curves show recent cohorts improving and older cohorts plateauing. PSL compliance is 40%. Bandhan intends to remain the segment leader — "we are the leader, and we will be the leader" — but capped at 33–35% of the book.
- **Wholesale banking (+38%, 33% of advances)** — deliberately margin-dilutive and defended as such. The strategy is wallet share, not spread: "the entry is through the advances… that is not our purpose." The bank entered **forex only last quarter** and is building cash management, LCs and trade finance to convert low-margin credit into fee income. Rates are claimed to be at or better than industry average, and the ecosystem play (corporate salary accounts, vendor payments) is the real objective.
- **Retail assets (+45%)** — CV, CE, auto and gold are the momentum products. Reported growth slowed because of one deliberate non-strategic decline (OD against term deposits); excluding it, the book grew a healthy 5% sequentially. **Gold loans declined** because implementing the RBI's new circular — "the entire circular was a 180-degree change" — disrupted sourcing from April to mid-May; normal sourcing has resumed.
- **Housing finance (22% of advances)** — declined slightly after a complete structural revamp into three verticals produced "teething problems."
- **Liabilities** — the deliberate bulk reduction is the story: bulk down 13% YoY to 26% of deposits from 32%, with 86% of what remains non-callable. Retail deposits and CASA both +16%.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Fee income** is the main remaining ROA lever — third-party distribution grew 47% YoY, processing fees recovered on higher disbursements (notably in EEB), and the wholesale ecosystem build (forex, cash management, LCs) is designed to convert thin-spread corporate credit into fee income.
- **Branch-channel asset sourcing** — from ~INR200cr/month to >INR900cr per quarter, replacing expensive DSA commissions. Contingent on the LOS (loan origination system) investment, after which "I can make all my branches as the sales point of retail and the housing assets" and even the ~4,400 banking units in metro and urban centres become sales points.
- **New products** — Legacy, Elite and Elite+ launched; corporate salary packages revamped; **credit card awaiting launch**.
- **EEB re-acceleration** — the growth is deliberately withheld, not unavailable. If the external environment improves, EEB can move to the top of the 5–10% band, which would be the fastest route back toward the original ROA aspiration.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Capital strength.** CAR 18.2% with Tier 1 at 17.5% — ample headroom to fund growth without dilution while the ROA journey plays out.
- **Deposit granularity is now genuinely improved**, not just claimed: retail deposits at 74% of total, bulk cut to 26%, and 86% of remaining bulk non-callable — which materially reduces liquidity volatility. LCR of 140% against a 94% CD ratio.
- **EEB franchise leadership** with a rebuilt underwriting stack — the yield advantage (EEB carries the highest yields in the book) is a real asset that is currently being deliberately under-used.
margins & cost dynamics:
NIM held at 6.2% but the trajectory broke. The mechanism management described: the FY26 repo cuts fed through to term-deposit costs with a lag, so the benefit landed in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 and **will not be available from Q2 onwards** — meanwhile competitors including large stable banks have started raising deposit rates despite no repo increase, because durable system liquidity is running near INR1 trillion against a need of ~INR2.5 trillion. Savings-bank cost of funds is already up ~20–25bps QoQ. Compounding this, EEB (the highest-yield book) is being deliberately grown slowly, so the 100bps February yield hike delivers rate but not volume — the CFO was explicit: "while the rate has gone up, the volume impact is not coming through."

On costs, opex rose 19% YoY on IT investment, annual salary revisions and performance payouts, plus the one-time INR61cr gratuity provision. **IT cost alone is up 65% YoY**, driven by multinational vendors raising prices on hardware, servers, cloud and AMC as Middle East disruption tightens chip supply. Management refused to slow the investment — "we cannot stop on that" — accepting near-term ROA dilution for capability. Cost-to-income sits near 62% and is expected to stay there for roughly a year.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Technology is the capex programme. The bank implemented core banking only three years ago; the current investment cycle is the **loan origination system (LOS)** plus work on CRS, alongside new product build-outs. IT is ~8% of opex (9.5% with depreciation), up from 5–6% two years ago. **Payback is guided at ~18 months**, with the pace of IT cost growth expected to taper thereafter. The concrete near-term deliverable is the **credit card launch in Q2 FY27**.
capital allocation: CAR of 18.2% and Tier 1 of 17.5% mean capital is not the constraint — growth is being paced by risk appetite and funding, not capital. Capital is being consumed by (i) secured book growth at 27%, (ii) technology, and (iii) balance-sheet clean-up (the ARC sale and technical write-off). Management explicitly chose transparency over optics on the guidance cut — repeating four separate times that it "wanted to be very clear and transparent to our investors."
risks & watch-items:
- **The guidance cut itself.** From 1.6–1.8% to 1.2–1.4% ROA at exit-Q4 FY27, with the original aspiration deferred to an unspecified later date. Analysts pushed hard on whether 1.1% (adjusted) can reach 1.4% when NIM cannot expand and credit cost is already at the guided range; the answer — 10–20bps from other income plus marginal credit-cost improvement — is a thin bridge.
- **Funding cost with no repo relief.** Competitors raising deposit rates into a liquidity shortfall; FCNR-B provided essentially nothing (INR30cr).
- **Energy crisis transmission to microfinance.** Management named this as the segment most exposed to an energy shock — "this segment cannot pass on" — and expects rationalised commercial gas cylinder availability to raise costs for EEB borrowers. Not yet showing as delinquency, and the credit-cost guidance was not changed, but it is the reason EEB growth is throttled.
- **SMA-0 in EEB rose to 3.5% from 3.1%.** Attributed to April holidays (three consecutive business days) plus the West Bengal elections. Management's supporting evidence is credible: SMA-1 slippage fell, so forward-rolling was arrested and balances stayed parked in SMA-0. Still, this is the number to watch.
- **Headline asset-quality improvement is partly engineered** — INR291cr ARC sale plus INR597cr technical write-off. The reported PCR of 71.1% (74.3% with SR provisions) is well below the 86% headline that includes technical write-offs.
- **IT cost inflation of 65% YoY** with an 18-month payback promise and no ability to push back on multinational vendors.
- **Wholesale banking dilutes NIM by design**, and an analyst pressed directly on whether giving up that growth would solve the margin problem. Management declined, betting on fee income instead — a bet that has not yet been proven.
- **Unpredictable monsoon**, flagged but with no visible impact yet.
management quality / tone: The defining feature of this call was voluntary, pre-emptive transparency. Partha Pratim Sengupta cut guidance in the prepared remarks rather than under questioning, quantified the cut precisely, and repeatedly separated external causes from internal execution — a distinction he is entitled to make, since credit cost, GNPA, collection efficiency, secured mix and deposit granularity all improved in the same quarter. He named the specific numbers behind the deterioration (savings cost +20–25bps, IT +65% YoY, opex-to-assets 4.3% vs 4.2%), and the CFO decomposed the 40bps into 30bps NIM and 10bps opex without being asked twice. Weaknesses: he did not really answer MB Mahesh's challenge on whether sacrificing wholesale growth would protect margin, and the bridge from an adjusted 1.1% to 1.4% ROA remains under-specified. The Digant Haria exchange — on high DSA commissions, collection agency costs and a secured book he characterised as "probably 0% ROA" — was the sharpest on the call, and the answer (LOS-enabled branch sourcing, INR200cr/month → INR900cr/quarter) was concrete but leaves cost-to-income flat for another year.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Every internally controllable metric improved while the external ones deteriorated. Credit cost 2.0% → 1.8%, EEB slippages INR690cr → INR604cr, GNPA to 3.1%, bulk deposits 32% → 26%, secured mix to 57%. The ROA cut is genuinely not an execution failure, which makes it a different kind of investment question — one about the rate cycle and geopolitics, not about the bank.
- The 100bps EEB yield hike is dormant firepower. Rate was taken in February but volume was withheld, so the margin benefit has not landed. If the external environment stabilises and EEB moves to the top of its 5–10% band, NIM upside arrives with a lag and without any new decision.
- Wholesale banking at 38% growth is deliberately NIM-dilutive and is the clearest strategic tension in the bank. It only pays off if forex, cash management and trade fee income materialise — the business was entered *last quarter*, so there is no track record yet.
- Recoveries and upgrades looked unusually strong this quarter partly because ~INR120cr of it was cash from the ARC deal, not organic. The CFO volunteered this when an analyst spotted the disconnect.
- IT at 8% of opex against a 10% mature-bank benchmark, with core banking only three years old, means Bandhan is mid-cycle on a catch-up build rather than over-investing. The stated glide path is 10% now, 8% later.
- Gold loan decline was regulatory implementation, not demand — a one-quarter artefact of the RBI circular that management expects to reverse from Q2.

- **EEB franchise leadership** with a rebuilt underwriting stack — the yield advantage (EEB carries the highest yields in the book) is a real asset that is currently being deliberately under-used.
margins & cost dynamics:

The bank implemented core banking only three years ago; the current investment cycle is the **loan origination system (LOS)** plus work on CRS, alongside new product build-outs. The concrete near-term deliverable is the **credit card launch in Q2 FY27**.
capital allocation: CAR of 18.2% and Tier 1 of 17.5% mean capital is not the constraint — growth is being paced by risk appetite and funding, not capital. Capital is being consumed by (i) secured book growth at 27%, (ii) technology, and (iii) balance-sheet clean-up (the ARC sale and technical write-off). risks & watch-items:
- **The guidance cut itself.** From 1.6–1.8% to 1.2–1.4% ROA at exit-Q4 FY27, with the original aspiration deferred to an unspecified later date. Analysts pushed hard on whether 1.1% (adjusted) can reach 1.4% when NIM cannot expand and credit cost is already at the guided range; the answer — 10–20bps from other income plus marginal credit-cost improvement — is a thin bridge.
- **Funding cost with no repo relief.** Competitors raising deposit rates into a liquidity shortfall; FCNR-B provided essentially nothing (INR30cr).
- **Energy crisis transmission to microfinance.** Management named this as the segment most exposed to an energy shock — "this segment cannot pass on" — and expects rationalised commercial gas cylinder availability to raise costs for EEB borrowers. Not yet showing as delinquency, and the credit-cost guidance was not changed, but it is the reason EEB growth is throttled.
- **SMA-0 in EEB rose to 3.5% from 3.1%.** Attributed to April holidays (three consecutive business days) plus the West Bengal elections. - **Headline asset-quality improvement is partly engineered** — INR291cr ARC sale plus INR597cr technical write-off. The reported PCR of 71.1% (74.3% with SR provisions) is well below the 86% headline that includes technical write-offs.
- **IT cost inflation of 65% YoY** with an 18-month payback promise and no ability to push back on multinational vendors.
- **Wholesale banking dilutes NIM by design**, and an analyst pressed directly on whether giving up that growth would solve the margin problem. Management declined, betting on fee income instead — a bet that has not yet been proven.
- **Unpredictable monsoon**, flagged but with no visible impact yet.
management quality / tone: The defining feature of this call was voluntary, pre-emptive transparency. hero.oneLiner: Operationally the best quarter Bandhan has had in a while — PAT INR502cr (+35%), credit cost down to 1.8% from 2.0%, GNPA at 3.1%, secured book now 57% of advances and non-EEB two-thirds of the loan book — yet management **cut its headline ROA guidance from 1.6–1.8% to 1.2–1.4% at exit-Q4 FY27**, attributing the entire 40bps reduction to external factors: ~30bps from funding costs killing the planned NIM expansion to 6.5%, and ~10bps from technology costs inflated by Middle East supply-chain disruption (IT spend up 65% YoY). business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Deck frames the bank as a "Universal Bank with diversified portfolio" offering "Comprehensive financial solutions across all lending segments", with the book split as EEB ₹ 526.4 bn (~34% share of book), Housing & Retail ₹ 506.4 bn (~33% share of book) and Wholesale Banking ₹ 512.8 bn (~33% share of book).
- Stated de-concentration of the legacy microfinance business: "Share of EEB (Group + SBAL) reduced from 39.5% in Jun'25 to 33.8% in Jun'26"; Non-EEB Book ₹ 1,029.1 bn (27.4% YoY & 2.6% QoQ).
- Geographic de-risking away from the East: Share Of Non-East 62.1% of advances (30 bps YoY & 19 bps QoQ, excludes PTC & IBPC) and Share Of Non-East 43.5% of retail deposits (-167 bps YoY & -154 bps QoQ).
- The deck sets out four named strategic objectives: Portfolio Diversification (Higher Secured Mix), Liability Resilience (Higher Retail Deposits Share), Strengthen Asset Quality, and Improve Profitability — the last described as "Embedding predictability in return ratios through balance sheet strengthening and conscious risk realignment".
- Scale claimed: Total Customers 31.8 mn; presence across 35 States and UTs.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **EEB / microfinance** — INR52,641cr, roughly flat, with the customary Q1 seasonal decline much shallower than prior years. Yields were hiked **100bps in February 2026** and not since. Management stressed a rebuilt operating model: "a new model has been put into place with a lot of guardrails and also new credit underwriting system." Vintage curves show recent cohorts improving and older cohorts plateauing. PSL compliance is 40%. Bandhan intends to remain the segment leader — "we are the leader, and we will be the leader" — but capped at 33–35% of the book.
- **Wholesale banking (+38%, 33% of advances)** — deliberately margin-dilutive and defended as such. The strategy is wallet share, not spread: "the entry is through the advances… that is not our purpose." The bank entered **forex only last quarter** and is building cash management, LCs and trade finance to convert low-margin credit into fee income. Rates are claimed to be at or better than industry average, and the ecosystem play (corporate salary accounts, vendor payments) is the real objective.
- **Retail assets (+45%)** — CV, CE, auto and gold are the momentum products. Reported growth slowed because of one deliberate non-strategic decline (OD against term deposits); excluding it, the book grew a healthy 5% sequentially. **Gold loans declined** because implementing the RBI's new circular — "the entire circular was a 180-degree change" — disrupted sourcing from April to mid-May; normal sourcing has resumed.
- **Housing finance (22% of advances)** — declined slightly after a complete structural revamp into three verticals produced "teething problems."
- **Liabilities** — the deliberate bulk reduction is the story: bulk down 13% YoY to 26% of deposits from 32%, with 86% of what remains non-callable. Retail deposits and CASA both +16%.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable. The forward-growth constraint is deliberate: EEB growth is being throttled at 5–10% because of external risk rather than demand, and management repeated that it will not repeat past mistakes — "we do not want to suddenly jump very aggressively what we have did in the past and then burnt our fingers." FCNR-B mobilisation, which the sector is counting on for funding relief, has been negligible here: **only INR30cr raised**.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **ROA — the headline change. Cut from 1.6–1.8% to 1.2–1.4% at exit-Q4 FY27.** The CFO broke the 40bps down explicitly: **~30bps from NIM** (the bank had "line of sight towards a 6.5% by the end of Q4FY27"; that is now abandoned) and **~10bps from opex** (opex-to-assets guided at 4.2%, already running 4.3%). The medium-term 1.6–1.8% aspiration is **retained but the timeline extended** — "the realization of this aspiration could extend beyond the time line we had originally envisaged."
- **NIM: hold ~6.2%.** No further upside is being built in — "it will be a great achievement for the bank to hold on to the NIMs that we have achieved during this particular quarter." Savings-bank cost of funds has already risen ~20–25bps QoQ despite no repo increase.
- **Credit cost: 1.6–1.8% guidance MAINTAINED** — explicitly not changed, with further marginal improvement expected. EEB credit cost at 3.3% is "very close to the guidance."
- **Credit growth FY27: 14% overall**, comprising **EEB 5–10%** and **non-EEB 20%+**. Q1 tracked ahead at 16% overall and 27% non-EEB; EEB is the laggard at flat.
- **Portfolio mix targets:** EEB capped at **33–35%** of the book; **40% unsecured / 60% secured**.
- **Other income: 10–20bps of ROA improvement expected** — one of only two identified levers left to close the gap to 1.4%.
- **Opex: 4.2% of assets** targeted (4.3% now). **IT cost to remain within 10% of opex** (currently ~8%, ~9.5% including depreciation, against a mature-bank benchmark of 10%), then "slowly bring it down to 8%" as it delivers value. **Cost-to-income (~62%) to stay flat for about a year and taper from FY28.**
- **Technology payback: ~18 months** — "after 18 months or so, we should see the outcome of all of this coming in the form of productivity gains."
- **Credit card launch expected in Q2 FY27** — "we are just waiting to be launched… probably in this quarter."
- **PSL compliance of the MFI book** (currently 40%) to be dialled up — "post this quarter, we will be comfortably placed in terms of PSL."
- **DSA dependency to fall as branch sourcing scales** — branch-channel asset sourcing has gone from ~INR200cr/month to **over INR900cr in the last quarter**.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Fee income** is the main remaining ROA lever — third-party distribution grew 47% YoY, processing fees recovered on higher disbursements (notably in EEB), and the wholesale ecosystem build (forex, cash management, LCs) is designed to convert thin-spread corporate credit into fee income.
- **Branch-channel asset sourcing** — from ~INR200cr/month to >INR900cr per quarter, replacing expensive DSA commissions. Contingent on the LOS (loan origination system) investment, after which "I can make all my branches as the sales point of retail and the housing assets" and even the ~4,400 banking units in metro and urban centres become sales points.
- **New products** — Legacy, Elite and Elite+ launched; corporate salary packages revamped; **credit card awaiting launch**.
- **EEB re-acceleration** — the growth is deliberately withheld, not unavailable. If the external environment improves, EEB can move to the top of the 5–10% band, which would be the fastest route back toward the original ROA aspiration.

- [EEB stress pool] EEB Stress-Pool Total ₹ 39.8 bn at Jun'26 versus ₹ 57.7 bn at Jun'25 (-31.0% YoY), with EEB Provisions Total ₹ 30.0 bn and "PCR % (Outstanding % on Stress pool)" of 75.4%; EEB NPA by geography at Jun'26 — West Bengal ₹ 10.2 bn (1.9%), Assam ₹ 4.6 bn (0.9%), Rest of India ₹ 4.8 bn (0.9%)? — see notes, this three-way geography series is a chart whose label bindings are ambiguous in the extract; Overall EEB NPA is stated as ₹ 31.0 bn / 5.9%.
- [Borrower leverage] Deck asserts "Majority of the borrowers with loan only with Bandhan or at max two lenders", "Strong focus towards orderly resolution of leveraged portfolio", "96% of the Portfolio" and "Sharp decrease in other Lenders QoQ" — the underlying Bandhan / Bandhan+1 / +2 / +3 / +4 / >4 percentage series cannot be reliably bound to its nine month-columns in this extract.
- [Credit ratings] Non-Convertible Debenture rated [ICRA]AA- (Stable) and CRISIL AA-/Stable (₹ 12.95 bn, ICRA rating for ₹ 0.75 bn only); Certificate of Deposit rated CRISIL A1+ and [ICRA] A1+ (₹ 60.00 bn, ICRA rating for ₹ 30 bn only); Security Receipts from the ARC portfolio sale rated RR2 ₹ 2.66 bn, RR3 ₹ 2.06 bn, RR4 ₹ 1.36 bn, Unrated ₹ 0.01 bn.
- [Governance] Non-Executive Chairman Debasish Panda (1987-batch IAS, former Chairman of IRDAI, former Director on the Boards of RBI, SBI, Bank of Baroda and LIC); MD & CEO Partha Pratim Sengupta (ex-Deputy MD and Chief Credit Officer at SBI, former MD & CEO of Indian Overseas Bank); an RBI (Nominee) Additional Director, Arun Kumar Singh, is on the board with an extended term "up to June 23, 2027, or till further orders, whichever is earlier".
- [Recognition] ET Edge Best BFSI Brands Award 2026 (9th Edition); 2025 Gallup Exceptional Workplace Award — "among the only 62 organisations worldwide", a two-time winner; DIGIXX Awards 2026 by Adgully for a digital lead-generation campaign.
